# OAuth verification abort rejects the verifier, cancels shared authentication and removes the queued prompt

Scope: ConfigVerifier.verifyConfig OAuth operation, after a prompt is queued and before credential completion, is aborted with an explicit reason. Trace the abort signal into OAuth2Module and the actual OAuth2 callback, pending-prompt removal, verification rejection, temporary-server cleanup, and exact browser_verifyConfig.js assertions.

This is one source-backed behavior chain at Thunderbird `87d0159c7149a43253964c2cb6917939557dc799` and Firefox `1a097ed8d31f6b307a5d0ebc34a82ceaf7f3727b`. The concrete test leaves `alter` undefined and aborts after the OAuth window loads, before submitting credentials. It proposes closure of this chain only. Independent review is pending.

## Trigger

The concrete test creates a separate AbortController and verifier. It starts IMAP verification with OAuth2, user at test.test, STARTTLS, and no alter argument. It waits for the internal OAuth window before checking the queue and aborting with one Error object. The entry point is real verifyConfig, not a replacement OAuth body.

Evidence: [mail/components/accountcreation/test/browser/browser_verifyConfig.js:214–243](https://github.com/mozilla/releases-comm-central/blob/87d0159c7149a43253964c2cb6917939557dc799/mail/components/accountcreation/test/browser/browser_verifyConfig.js#L214-L243).

## Verification state

verifyConfig creates a temporary incoming server, stores config and resolve/reject callbacks, sets the auth and connection fields, then calls verifyLogon. The public promise normally resolves to the successful configuration; this abort path rejects. verifyLogon passes this exact verifier as nsIUrlListener and clears the URL msgWindow to suppress password prompts. The IMAP native service creates an IMAP URL and registers that same listener.

## Actual native oauth owner

The IMAP protocol selects XOAUTH2 for the OAuth2 auth preference and creates OAuth2ThreadHelper. The helper creates the registered OAuth2Module, initializes it from the same server, then releases its server reference. At authentication, the actual listener passed to OAuth2Module.connect is this native helper. No callback target is inferred from its name.

## Queue and async contract

OAuth2Module.connect delegates to _fetchAccessToken with SASL formatting requested. The module listener uses a normal method for onPromptStartAsync, so this is the promptListener object there; its onPromptAuthAvailable arrow retains the OAuth2Module receiver. It queues under login origin plus username. The first listener starts OAuth2.connect and later signals Boolean completion. Equal-key requests append consumers and do not start another prompt.

## Queue owner and dispatch

The service owns pendingPrompts entries and their first listener and consumers. RunnablePrompter retains the service and key. doAsyncAuthPrompt increments the active count before dispatch. Firefox nsIEventTarget defines DISPATCH_NORMAL as queued later processing and documents dispatch failure during shutdown; there is no local rollback around dispatch. This is a read interface boundary, not a claim to have analyzed the entire event loop.

## Oauth object sharing

A later cleanup module is not the original module. initFromMail derives the same host, user and server type. initFromHostname reuses a live weak-cache OAuth2 object only when origin, authorization endpoint, username and required-scope containment match. The test provider maps test.test IMAP to test_mail and an internal-browser issuer. The module owns _oauth strongly; the module-level cache owns only WeakRef entries.

## Authorization operation

OAuth2.connect creates and stores its promise, resolve and reject callbacks. With no usable token and allowed UI it starts authorization. Other exits reject for UI forbidden, another window, or cooldown. requestAuthorization resets _authorizationReceived, registers the quit observer, selects InternalRequest for this provider, and starts it. The request opens browserRequest.xhtml with the request object in window arguments.

## Window listener owner

browserRequest.js installs load and close handlers. loadRequestedUrl retrieves the request from window.arguments, loads its URL and calls request.loaded with the actual window and browser.webProgress. InternalRequest.loaded stores an owned listener object, registers it for progress, and retains the window. Its cleanup removes that exact progress listener, closes the window and deletes the window field. close marks the request inactive, so close-event reportUserClosed calling cancelled does not cancel again.

## Abort cross repository

The JavaScript AbortController is implemented in Firefox. Abort saves the aborted state and calls SignalAbort with the supplied reason. SignalAbort stores that exact JS reason before dispatching an abort event. ConfigVerifier receives the event through its once listener and calls SetUrlState(false, NS_ERROR_ABORT) on the running URL. This does not directly reject the OAuth promise.

## Url callback to cleanup

The IMAP running URL first reports its running state, which gives ConfigVerifier._runningUrl its value. nsMsgMailNewsUrl::SetUrlState changes state, invokes each registered OnStopRunningUrl and clears the listeners. ConfigVerifier sets _runningUrl null. The test has no alter argument and no certificate error; its failure branch reaches _failed. _failed calls cleanup before rejecting with signal.reason.

## Cancel shared operation

cleanup removes the abort listener, initializes a second matching OAuth2Module, and checks the actual pending key. If present, it requests a token with two no-op callbacks, which appends a queue consumer. It then calls cancelPrompt on the shared OAuth2 object. cancelPrompt first calls onAuthorizationFailed with data={} and reason cancelled, then finishAuthorizationRequest. The former rejects OAuth2.connect with that object; it does not pass the test Error to OAuth.

## Cancel window and observer

finishAuthorizationRequest clears the endpoint connecting flag, removes the quit observer, closes the request and nulls the request field. InternalRequest.close disables itself and runs the installed listener cleanup. This is initiated cleanup; window.close is not a returned promise for actual window destruction. If authorization code has already been received, onAuthorizationFailed ignores the cancelled rejection; that late-cancel branch is distinct from this test, which aborts at the displayed login page before submitting credentials.

## Actual failure consumer

OAuth2Module handles OAuth promise rejection by calling the native helper listener.onFailure(NS_ERROR_ABORT), then callback.onAuthResult(false). The helper ignores the numeric error for token delivery, passes an empty string to CompleteConnect, and returns NS_OK. CompleteConnect accepts only the first result, stores it under a monitor, sets completion and wakes the IMAP waiter. GetXOAuth2String then returns the empty token. The protocol releases its helper reference and returns NS_ERROR_FAILURE for the empty token, so it sends no AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2 token in that branch.

## Queue completion

The Boolean callback resolves #promiseAuthPrompt. run deletes the pending key before notifying consumers, sends onPromptCanceled on false, decrements the active count and attempts the next queue item. The cleanup consumer calls its no-op failure handler. Normal run completion resolves undefined; it does not mean the next prompt, native thread shutdown or all window destruction has completed.

## Temporary server cleanup

After initiating OAuth cancellation, cleanup calls removeIncomingServer(server,true) and clears its field on normal return. The native account manager logs out the server, removes its map entry, notifies folder/server consumers, requests file removal, sends message-server-removed and clears values. File-removal failures are logged rather than returned. Shutdown closes cached connections; each IMAP connection receives TellThreadToDie(true), which removes the connection, sets death flags, closes the transport with NS_ERROR_ABORT and wakes its URL monitor. This requests native shutdown, not a joined-thread completion guarantee.

## Exception and retention limits

cleanup wraps all cleanup work in one try/catch: an exception before server removal can skip removal and field clearing, while _failed still rejects with the abort reason after cleanup returns. OAuth promise failure invokes listener.onFailure before onAuthResult; this actual native receiver returns NS_OK. For other receivers, a thrown onFailure can skip queue settlement. run has no finally: login initialization failure or a throwing first.onPromptCanceled can leave count/entry intact. The test does not inject those failures. The native helper also has a shutdown callback capturing self; dropping the protocol reference therefore does not prove immediate destruction. Its destructor releases the module on the main thread.
